A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and scientific appendices support reliable comparison. The NeurIPS checklist missing from v3 is an identifiable deletion, not an extraction gap.

before.justification: Section 5 and the appendices report original clustering, typicality-correlation, and compression analyses of LLM embeddings against human categorization datasets.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical analyses, including model-level results in Tables 1–2 and Figures 1–8.

M1.justification: The static token-embedding extraction, k-means clustering, cosine-similarity analysis, and complexity-plus-distortion objective remain unchanged in Sections 3.2–5.

E1.justification: Both versions use Rosch (1973), Rosch (1975), and McCloskey and Glucksberg (1978) for the same categorical-alignment, typicality, and compression tasks. No dataset, language, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The same model entries and human-category/random-clustering comparisons are retained in Section 5 and Tables 1–2. Misra et al. (2021) is newly cited but is not added as an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Both retain the same embedding inputs, model configurations, category-matched or swept cluster counts, AMI/NMI/ARI and Spearman metrics, and beta = 1 for the compression objective. No reported experimental setting changes.

E4.justification: The supplementary clustering metrics in A.3, typicality scatter plots in A.6, and compression analyses across cluster counts in A.8 are retained unchanged. No ablation, robustness test, or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both specify 100 random k-means initializations with averaged results and retain Figure 6's error bars and Table 2's p < 0.05 significance markers. Checklist removal deletes a generic reporting assertion, without changing the documented statistical procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and Figures 1–8 retain the same entries, values, curves, and findings. For example, BERT-large-uncased's Table 2 correlations remain -0.427, -0.198, and 0.206 for Rosch (1973), Rosch (1975), and McCloskey (1978), respectively.

T1.justification: Section 4's mathematical definitions, assumptions, and Equations (1)–(4) are unchanged. Appendix A.7 retains the same derivations for singleton clusters and a single cluster containing all items.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the framework and dataset-digitization contributions, broad category-alignment claim, limited typicality-alignment claim, and claimed divergence between LLM compression and human conceptual richness.

C2.justification: The interpretations in Sections 5–6 and all five limitations in Appendix A are retained, including restrictions concerning language, human benchmarks, model scope, static representations, and textual input. Checklist removal does not remove a distinct scientific interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 replaces the anonymous dataset-link placeholder with a concrete Hugging Face URL for the CSV dataset. Checklist removal also removes the promise to release code and data upon acceptance. Other technical descriptions are unchanged; the PDFs do not establish whether the linked resource is accessible.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography add Misra, Ettinger, and Rayz (2021), 'Do language models learn typicality judgments from text?' The surrounding research-gap argument and other cited works remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 removes the NeurIPS checklist between the references and Appendix A and makes limited citation and access-text edits. The scientific narrative and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added reference and dataset URL cause limited text reflow, and the arXiv margin stamp is updated. Checklist pages are removed. Figures 1–8 and Tables 1–2 retain identical graphical content, captions, and layouts.

improvement.justification: Replacing the anonymous dataset placeholder with a concrete access location in A.1 improves reproducibility documentation, while the added citation acknowledges relevant typicality research. These limited gains outweigh the loss of the checklist's prospective code-release assurance. Methods, empirical evidence, and scientific limitations remain unchanged; actual resource availability is not established by the PDFs.
